prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Pixel-art weapon source atlas for PIPE WRENCH exclusive to Tony in retro SNES side-scrolling plumbing game. Compact teal handle with silver steel hooked adjustable serrated jaw, chunky navy outline, crisp pixel clusters, consistent recognizable tool in every pose. Exactly 3 columns x 3 rows, equal square cells on transparent square canvas. Weapon only, no hands or character. Row1: inventory icon diagonal wrench; held ready wrench aimed diagonally up-right; windup wrench tilted back up-left. Row2: strike wrench extended horizontally RIGHT jaw leading; follow-through wrench diagonally down-right; isolated pale cyan curved sweep arc effect. Row3: small white-yellow contact spark; expanded angular white-yellow contact burst; dissipating tiny sparks. Maintain identical tool scale for held/windup/strike/followthrough, same grip pivot relative to cell center, ample padding around all art. All 9 sprites wholly contained and separated by generous transparent gutters. No text, labels, numbers, grid, background, haze or shadows. Genuine alpha transparency. Opaque pixel-art interiors. Tool design: compact teal-handled pipe wrench for quick horizontal sweep, not an open-ended spanner.

integration_notes: Source sheet is visually reviewed, not a validated runtime atlas.
Generated sprites can cross nominal cell edges; inspect and isolate regions before import.
Measure per-frame grip pivots and muzzle sockets; preserve one weapon scale across held poses.
Do not fit every frame to its opaque bounds; that changes tool scale and grip alignment.
Existing character sheets include baked-in weapons. Clean hand/body layers are needed before attaching these tools.
Mirror held sprites for left-facing play; effects should use their contact or muzzle origin.
Visual effects do not define collision, damage, reach, travel distance, or blast radius.
Clean alpha fringes and validate readable icons and effects at gameplay size.
